content:
Understanding Quadrilaterals is two skills in one. First, find angles with two short formulas. Second, know the family tree — every square is a rhombus, but a rhombus need not be a square. The IMO tests both, again and again. Take the free IMO Class 8 Quadrilaterals online test below before any revision. Ten MCQs, instant score, full explanations — it will tell you exactly what to fix first.

What the IMO asks from Quadrilaterals in Class 8

  • Interior angle sum of a polygon: (n − 2) × 180°.
  • Exterior angles — always 360° in total, for any polygon.
  • Regular polygons: each interior and each exterior angle.
  • Parallelogram facts: sides, angles, diagonals.
  • The special shapes: rhombus, rectangle, square, kite, trapezium.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Exterior angles of any convex polygon add to 360°. So a regular n-gon has each exterior angle 360/n.
  • In a parallelogram, adjacent angles add to 180°. Opposite angles are equal.
  • Diagonals tell the shapes apart. Rhombus: they cross at 90°. Rectangle: they are equal. Square: both.
  • A kite has two pairs of equal ADJACENT sides. It is not a parallelogram.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Using (n − 2) × 180° on a question about exterior angles.
  • Assuming the diagonals of a parallelogram are equal. Only a rectangle promises that.
  • Calling a shape with four equal sides a square. Without right angles, it is a rhombus.

questions.q: A convex polygon has all its interior angles less than 180 degrees. If a polygon has exactly one interior angle that is greater than 180 degrees, what type of polygon is it?
questions.explanation: A polygon is classified as concave (or non-convex) if at least one interior angle exceeds 180 degrees (a reflex angle). A convex polygon has ALL interior angles strictly less than 180 degrees. Since this polygon has exac

questions.q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon measures 40 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: The sum of all exterior angles of any convex polygon is 360 degrees. For a regular polygon, each exterior angle = 360/n. So 360/n = 40, which gives n = 360/40 = 9.

questions.q: In a regular polygon, each interior angle is 5 times its exterior angle. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Let the exterior angle be E. Then interior angle = 5E. Since interior + exterior = 180 degrees, 5E + E = 180, so 6E = 180, giving E = 30 degrees. Number of sides = 360/30 = 12.

questions.q: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 2520 degrees. How many diagonals does this polygon have?
Four angles of a pentagon measure 80 degrees, 100 degrees, 120 degrees, and 140 degrees. What is the fifth angle?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles of a pentagon = (5 - 2) × 180 = 540 degrees. Fifth angle = 540 - (80 + 100 + 120 + 140) = 540 - 440 = 100 degrees.

questions.q: In a convex polygon, three of the interior angles are each 120 degrees, and the remaining interior angles are each 160 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Let the polygon have n sides. Sum of interior angles = (n - 2) × 180. So 3(120) + (n - 3)(160) = (n - 2)(180). Expanding: 360 + 160n - 480 = 180n - 360. Simplifying: 160n - 120 = 180n - 360. So 240 = 20n, giving n = 12.

questions.q: In a convex polygon, the number of diagonals exceeds the number of sides by 12. How many vertices does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: n(n - 3)/2 - n = 12. Multiply by 2: n(n - 3) - 2n = 24, so n² - 3n - 2n = 24, giving n² - 5n - 24 = 0. Factoring: (n - 8)(n + 3) = 0. Since n must be positive, n = 8.

questions.q: In a parallelogram ABCD, AB = 8 cm and the perimeter is 30 cm. Find the length of AD.
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal, so AB = CD = 8 cm and AD = BC. Perimeter = 2(AB + AD) = 30. So AB + AD = 15, giving AD = 15 - 8 = 7 cm.

questions.q: ABCD is a rhombus with angle A = 60 degrees. Find angle B.
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so consecutive angles are supplementary. Angle B = 180 - 60 = 120 degrees.

questions.q: A parallelogram has adjacent sides of length 7 cm and 11 cm. If one diagonal measures 14 cm, find the length of the other diagonal.
questions.explanation: By the parallelogram law, d1² + d2² = 2(a² + b²). So 14² + d2² = 2(7² + 11²) = 2(49 + 121) = 2(170) = 340. Thus 196 + d2² = 340, giving d2² = 144, and d2 = 12 cm.
